🎯 Psychotic Disorders & Antipsychotic Pharmacology — High-Yield One-Pager

Psychotic Disorders & Antipsychotic Pharmacology — condensed pre-exam summary

Psychosis — Core Definition

  • Loss of touch with reality testing; never normal, seen in all cultures
  • Need ≥1: hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior (incl. catatonia), negative symptoms
  • Illusion = misperceived real stimulus ≠ hallucination (no stimulus)

4 Dopamine Tracts

  • Mesolimbic ↑ → positive symptoms
  • Mesocortical ↓ → negative symptoms
  • Nigrostriatal blockade → EPS
  • Tuberoinfundibular blockade → ↑prolactin

Timeline Trio

  • Brief psychotic: 1 day – 1 month
  • Schizophreniform: 1 – 6 months
  • Schizophrenia: > 6 months (+ postmorbid decline, 2+ of 5 A–E criteria)

Schizoaffective vs. Delusional D/O

  • Schizoaffective: baseline psychosis + mood episodes, PLUS ≥2wk psychosis-alone window
  • Delusional D/O: plausible fixed delusion, preserved function, no insight into the delusion only
  • 6 delusion subtypes: persecutory, somatic, erotomanic, grandiose, jealous, mixed

Typical vs. Atypical

  • Typical: D > S blockade; high/med/low potency
  • Atypical: S > D blockade
  • High potency = high EPS / low ACH; Low potency = low EPS / high ACH

PINES vs. DONES

  • -pines (olanzapine, quetiapine, asenapine): sedating, metabolic risk
  • -dones (risperidone, ziprasidone, paliperidone, iloperidone): "watered-down typicals," more EPS
  • PIPs = aripiprazole family (partial agonists); RIP = clozapine (last resort)

EPS Timeline & Tx

  • Dystonia (acute) → IM anticholinergic
  • Akathisia (acute/subacute) → propranolol
  • Pseudoparkinsonism (acute/subacute) → anticholinergic/amantadine
  • Tardive dyskinesia (chronic) → withdraw/switch agent (NOT anticholinergics)
  • D2 occupancy: ~70% efficacy threshold, ~78–80% EPS threshold

Receptor → Side Effect

  • H1 → sedation
  • α1 → orthostatic hypotension
  • M1 → dry mouth/blurred vision/urinary retention
  • D2 (nigrostriatal) → EPS
  • D2 (tuberoinfundibular) → galactorrhea/amenorrhea/gynecomastia

Clozapine — Gold Standard

  • Most effective; only proven-antisuicidal antipsychotic
  • Unique risks: agranulocytosis (1–2%), seizures, sialorrhea, myocarditis
  • No EPS/TD; mandatory ANC/WBC REMS monitoring
  • Superior in CUtLASS Band 2 (treatment-resistant disease)

Acute Agitation

  • "B-52": Benadryl 50mg + Haldol 5mg + Ativan 2mg IM, PRN
  • NMS red flag: rigidity + hyperthermia + diaphoresis → stop the antipsychotic first

Smoking & CYP1A2

  • Smoking induces CYP1A2 → ↓ clozapine/olanzapine levels
  • Quitting/hospitalization removes induction → levels can rise ~50%
  • Resuming smoking after discharge → breakthrough psychosis despite compliance

Key Numbers

  • Relapse: 20%/yr oral vs. ~5%/yr LAI vs. 70% (1yr) / 90% (2yr) unmedicated
  • 95% of psychotic-disorder patients smoke
  • Diabetes risk 2–4× baseline in psychiatric patients on APs
  • NMS mortality/dementia boxed warning: 1.6–1.7× death risk

First-Line Consensus

  • 1st: SGA (all 5 major guideline bodies agree)
  • 2nd: SGA/FGA
  • 3rd: Clozapine
  • 4th: Clozapine augmentation
  • CATIE: FGA (perphenazine) ≈ SGA for routine use, more cost-effective

Side-Effect Rankings — Lowest → Highest Risk (Master Reference)

  • Metabolic syndrome: lowest = Abilify/Geodon/Latuda/Vraylar; highest = Zyprexa/Clozaril
  • QT prolongation: lowest = Latuda/Abilify; highest (typicals) = thioridazine/mesoridazine; highest (atypical) = ziprasidone
  • Prolactin elevation: lowest = aripiprazole/clozapine; highest = paliperidone/risperidone
  • Any EPS: lowest = clozapine/olanzapine/quetiapine; highest = chlorpromazine/haloperidol
  • Orthostatic hypotension: lowest = aripiprazole/asenapine/olanzapine/ziprasidone; highest = quetiapine/clozapine
  • Sedation: lowest = paliperidone/iloperidone/aripiprazole; highest = chlorpromazine/clozapine
  • Weight gain most: clozapine & olanzapine
  • T2DM risk most: clozapine & olanzapine
  • Agranulocytosis: unique to clozapine (1–2%)
  • Galactorrhea: risperidone/paliperidone & high-potency typicals
  • Antisuicidal: clozapine (antipsychotics); lithium (mood stabilizers) — only two psychiatric drugs with this property
  • Smoking/CYP1A2: affects clozapine & olanzapine specifically

🎯 Anxiety, OCD & Trauma-Related Disorders — High-Yield One-Pager

Anxiety, OCD & Trauma-Related Disorders — condensed pre-exam summary

DSM-5's 3 Chapters

  • Anxiety Disorders (separation anx., mutism, phobia, social anx., panic, GAD)
  • OCD & Related Disorders (OCD, BDD, hoarding, trichotillomania, excoriation)
  • Trauma & Stressor-Related (RAD, DSED, PTSD, acute stress, adjustment d/o)

Separation Anxiety & Mutism

  • Sep. anxiety: 4% of kids, F>M, familial; feigns illness; find the trigger
  • Selective mutism: mute in ONE venue, normal elsewhere, ≥1 month

Specific Phobia

  • 9% prevalence; animal→childhood, blood-injury→adolescence, other→20s
  • Systematic desensitization (graded+relaxation) vs. flooding (massive exposure)
  • Agoraphobia now unlinked from panic disorder in DSM-5

Panic Disorder

  • Attack: abrupt, peaks 30sec–5min, ≥4 of 13 symptoms
  • Disorder = attack + ≥1mo worry/behavior change
  • ALWAYS rule out MI/PE/arrhythmia before calling it panic

GAD

  • >6 months, ≥3 of 6 symptoms (1 in kids), hard to control
  • GAD-7 ≥10 → probable diagnosis; 5/10/15 = mild/mod/severe anchors

OCD

  • 4th most common psychiatric dx; ego-dystonic; ≥1hr/day or impairment
  • Needs MAX-dose SSRI (higher than depression dosing); clomipramine alt.
  • OCD (ego-dystonic) vs. OCPD (ego-syntonic) — the key discriminator
  • "Terrible triad": OCD + ADHD + Tourette

OCD-Spectrum

  • BDD: imagined/minor defect, huge preoccupation; more common in gay men
  • Hoarding, trichotillomania, excoriation: all new-ish dx, all Tx'd w/ serotonergics + CBT

PTSD

  • 7.8% lifetime; 5% men / 10.4% women
  • A-Stressor, B-Intrusion, C-Avoidance, D-Neg. cognition/mood, E-Arousal, F->1mo, G-Impairment, H-Exclusion

Acute Stress & Adjustment D/O

  • ASD = "brief psychotic disorder" of anxiety: 3 days–1 month, then → PTSD
  • Adjustment d/o: MOST common psych dx overall; within 3mo of stressor, resolves <6mo after it ends

Benzodiazepines

  • GABA-A agonist (NOT GABA-B — that's baclofen)
  • Absorption: rapid (diazepam/alprazolam) → intermediate (lorazepam) → slow (oxazepam/clonazepam)
  • LOT = Lorazepam/Oxazepam/Temazepam — no active metabolites, safest in liver dz/elderly
  • Dependence in as little as 2 weeks; limit use <4 months; PRN only for most indications

Other Anxiolytics

  • Buspirone: 5-HT1A partial agonist, delayed onset (weeks), "like water" post-benzo
  • Hydroxyzine: H1 inverse agonist, no abuse potential, watch QTc
  • Prazosin: first-line for PTSD nightmares specifically
  • Beta-blockers: performance-only social phobia, panic

Key Warnings

  • Never combine benzo + alcohol/opiates (resp. depression)
  • Flumazenil reverses OD but risks precipitating withdrawal/seizures
  • Paroxetine withdrawal can be worse than original anxiety — redose then taper
  • Elderly: lower benzo doses (↑Vd from lipophilicity + body fat)

Treatment by Disorder — Quick Reference

  • Separation anxiety: therapy + family therapy; serotonergic antidepressant if needed
  • Specific phobia: exposure therapy (systematic desensitization/flooding)
  • Social anxiety (generalized): SSRI, buspirone, CBT/assertiveness training
  • Social anxiety (performance-only): beta-blocker PRN
  • Panic disorder: SSRI/SNRI + short-term PRN benzo
  • Agoraphobia: same as panic disorder + beta-blockers
  • GAD: SSRI/SNRI, buspirone, mirtazapine; rare PRN benzo
  • OCD: MAX-dose SSRI/SNRI or clomipramine
  • PTSD: SSRI first-line; prazosin for nightmares specifically
  • Acute stress d/o: immediate therapy/counseling (not single-session debriefing)
  • Adjustment disorder: remove stressor + CBT/psychodynamic/supportive therapy
  • Comorbid schizophrenia + anxiety: high-potency benzo + antipsychotic

🎯 Legal Psychiatric Medicine — High-Yield One-Pager

Legal Psychiatric Medicine — condensed pre-exam summary

Confidentiality & Exceptions

  • Default rule, implicit, release only w/ patient authorization or legal compulsion
  • Asymmetry: can't take info from outsiders w/o consent; outsiders can give it freely
  • 6 exceptions: Tarasoff, involuntary hospitalization, supervision, emergency, incompetence/guardian, mandatory reporting
  • Privilege survives the patient's death; HIV warning is ethically OK, get legal input first

HIPAA (1996)

  • Privacy Rule = all PHI (paper/electronic/spoken); Security Rule = electronic PHI only
  • No authorization needed for Treatment/Payment/healthcare Operations (TPO)
  • Right to records EXCLUDES psychotherapy notes
  • States may enact stricter rules than the federal floor

Tarasoff Doctrine

  • I = duty to warn; II = duty to protect (broader)
  • Trigger: imminent/probable danger to a specific identifiable victim
  • Try least restrictive first: meds → family → visit frequency → hospitalize
  • Fantasies alone aren't reportable — must be judged as likely to be acted on

Capacity, Competence & Med Objection

  • Capacity = clinical/task-specific (psychiatrist decides); Competence = legal (courts decide)
  • 4 standards / "CARD": communicate, appreciate facts, reason, demonstrate understanding
  • No capacity + no surrogate → treat per patient's best interest
  • Advance directives: living will + healthcare proxy (active only once capacity lost); no directive → spouse → adult children → parents → siblings
  • Competence to stand trial (Dusky v. US): understand charges + assist attorney. Involuntary commitment bases: police power + parens patriae
  • Involuntary hospitalization ≠ incompetent to refuse meds — must prove incapacity + best interest; emergency overrides right to refuse

Malpractice — 4 D's

  • Duty → Deviation → Damages → Direct Causation — all 4 required
  • Best suicide-malpractice defense = documented ongoing risk assessment, not a safety contract
  • Family monitoring promises don't transfer physician responsibility

Ethical Dilemmas — Quick Hits

  • Never sex w/ current patients; psychiatrists: never with current OR former
  • Bequests to psychiatrists = unethical; recording needs informed consent; fee splitting illegal
  • Charging for missed visits = OK; APA bars psychiatrists from executions
  • Goldwater Rule: general expertise OK, no diagnosing public figures without exam + consent

Seclusion & Restraint

  • Only for immediate physical safety — never coercion, discipline, or convenience
  • Written MD/DO(/NP) order, regularly reviewed, time-limited, stopped ASAP
  • Medication used to subdue = chemical restraint

Consent & Termination

  • Informed consent: procedure, alternatives (even unaffordable ones), risks, benefits, right to withdraw
  • WIPE exceptions: Waiver, legally Incompetent, Therapeutic Privilege, Emergency
  • Minors: "Sex, Drugs, Rock and Roll" + legal emancipation + psychiatric emergencies; abortion is the exception to the exceptions
  • All STIs reportable except genital herpes (HSV-2)
  • Proper termination: certified letter, reason/date, emergency coverage, referrals, records, adequate time

Ethics & Forensics Terms — Quick Reference

  • Paternalism: acting for someone's benefit without their consent
  • Fiduciary duty: duty to act in the patient's best interest
  • Mens rea / actus reus: evil intent + voluntary conduct, both required for guilt
  • Substituted judgment: surrogate decides based on what the patient would have wanted
  • Respondeat superior: highest person in hierarchy is legally responsible for those below
  • Respect for autonomy: patient's right to self-determination, free of coercion
  • Altruism: putting others' needs before your own
  • Beneficence: obligation to relieve suffering
  • Non-malfeasance: duty to do no harm
  • Justice: equitable distribution of social wealth/benefits
  • Parens patriae: state acts as surrogate parent for those who can't care for themselves
  • M'Naughton Rule: NGRI if illness prevented understanding nature/quality/wrongness of the act
  • Durable power of attorney: advance-selected substitute decision-maker for incompetence
  • McGarry Instrument: 13-area guide for competence to stand trial
  • Sex-offender treatment: can be court-mandated; court becomes surrogate decision-maker in this domain

🎯 Personality Disorders — High-Yield One-Pager

Personality Disorders — condensed pre-exam summary

Foundations

  • Trait = normal variation. Disorder = pervasive + inflexible + maladaptive cluster of traits
  • Ego-syntonic: no insight, "world is the problem not me," rarely self-presents
  • Onset traceable to adolescence or earlier — never develops fresh mid-life
  • Diagnosis often requires collateral history (spouse/family confirming lifelong pattern)

3 Clusters

  • A = "Weird" (odd/eccentric): Paranoid, Schizoid, Schizotypal — share negative sx of schizophrenia
  • B = "Wild" (dramatic/erratic): Antisocial, Borderline, Histrionic, Narcissistic
  • C = "Worried" (anxious/fearful): Avoidant, Dependent, OCPD — share anxious symptomatology

Cluster A Mnemonics

  • Paranoid — GET FACT (grudges, exploitation, trust doubted, fidelity questioned, attacks perceived, confides rarely, threats read in)
  • Schizoid — SIR SAFE (solitary, indifferent, relationships/sex/activities/friends lacking, emotionally cold)
  • Schizotypal — UFO AIDER (unusual perceptions, friendless, odd beliefs, affect odd, ideas of reference, doubts others, eccentric, reluctant)

Cluster B Mnemonics

  • Antisocial — CALLOUS MAN (conduct d/o <15, arrests, lies, no superego, obligations unmet, unstable, unsafe, money problems, aggressive)
  • Borderline — I RAISED A PAIN (identity, relationships unstable, abandonment avoided, impulsive, suicidal gestures, empty, dissociative, affect unstable, paranoid ideation, anger, idealize/devalue, negativistic)
  • Histrionic — I CRAVE SIN (inappropriate/seductive, center of attention, relationships overestimated, appearance-focused, vulnerable to suggestion, exaggerated emotion, shifting/shallow, impressionistic speech, novelty craved)
  • Narcissistic — A FAME GAME (admiration, fantasizes success, arrogant, manipulative, envious, grandiose, associates w/ special people, me-first, empathy lacking)

Cluster C Mnemonics

  • Avoidant — RIDICULE (restrained, inhibited, disapproval expected, inadequate self-view, criticism expected, unwilling to get involved, longs for attachment, embarrassment feared)
  • Dependent — DARN HURT (disagreement hard, advice needed, responsibility delegated, nurturance sought, helpless alone, unrealistic self-care worry, relationships desperately sought, tasks hard to initiate)
  • OCPD — LOW MIRTH (leisure minimal, organization focus, work predominates, miserly, inflexible morals, rigid/stubborn, task completion impaired, hoards)

Key Differentiators

  • Schizoid (doesn't want relationships) vs. Avoidant (wants them, fears rejection)
  • OCD (true obsessions/compulsions, ego-dystonic) vs. OCPD (none, ego-syntonic)
  • BPD (rapid/reactive mood shifts, interpersonal triggers) vs. Bipolar (sustained autonomous episodes)
  • Histrionic (drama/attention) vs. Narcissistic (grandiosity/superiority)

Borderline PD Specifics

  • Name = "borderline" of depression and psychosis; micropsychotic/dissociative episodes under stress
  • Self-harm = para-suicidal (physical pain distracts from emotional pain), NOT usually suicidal intent
  • Ask: "Do you feel empty inside?" — classic affirmative response
  • Splitting: idealization → devaluation, black/white relationship view

Antisocial PD Specifics

  • = Sociopathy / psychopathy (lay terms)
  • REQUIRES documented conduct disorder before age 15 + current age ≥18
  • No superego; no remorse; externalizes all blame

Treatment

  • NO FDA-approved medication for ANY of the 10 personality disorders
  • DBT = specifically for BPD; CBT = mainstay for the other 9
  • "If DBT's an option, choose it; if not, choose CBT"
  • BPD polypharmacy: >50% on 2 psychotropics, >11% on 5+; quetiapine 82% vs 48% placebo response (Zanarini scale)
  • Meds target symptoms (depression, irritability, psychosis) — never the core disorder itself

All 10 at a Glance

  • Paranoid: distrust, malicious-motive assumption, grudges
  • Schizoid: genuinely prefers solitude, blunted affect
  • Schizotypal: unusual perceptions, magical thinking, odd speech
  • Antisocial: disregards rights of others, no remorse, conduct d/o hx
  • Borderline: unstable identity/relationships, abandonment fear, self-harm
  • Histrionic: attention-seeking, theatrical, shallow/shifting emotion
  • Narcissistic: grandiosity, entitlement, lacks empathy
  • Avoidant: wants relationships but fears rejection/ridicule
  • Dependent: clingy, needs excessive care/reassurance, indecisive
  • OCPD: rigid perfectionism, no true obsessions/compulsions, ego-syntonic

🎯 Sexual, Somatoform & Dissociative Disorders — High-Yield One-Pager

Sexual, Somatoform & Dissociative Disorders — condensed pre-exam summary

The Master Split

  • Unconscious production: somatic symptom, illness anxiety, conversion disorder
  • Conscious production: malingering, factitious disorder
  • Decision tree: conscious deceit? No → somatoform. Yes → goal external (2° gain) = malingering; goal psychological/sick role (1° gain) = factitious

Unconscious Disorders

  • Somatic symptom disorder: multi-system complaints, months-years
  • Illness anxiety disorder: fear of illness despite reassurance, minimal symptoms
  • Conversion disorder: sudden sensory/motor loss + la belle indifférence

Conscious Disorders

  • Malingering: external gain; stops once gain achieved; avoids procedures
  • Factitious disorder: sick role (primary gain); welcomes procedures
  • Munchausen = chronic factitious, physical signs, many hospitalizations
  • Munchausen by proxy = caregiver-induced illness in child/elder = ABUSE, must report

Dissociative Identity Disorder

  • ≥2 distinct personality states + recurrent amnesia gaps
  • Etiology: severe early childhood trauma (physical/sexual/emotional abuse)
  • Alter patterns: mutually aware / mutually unaware / one-way awareness
  • Ongoing debate: distinct entity vs. severe/chronic PTSD with dissociative traits

Amnesia, Fugue & Depersonalization

  • Dissociative amnesia: localized/selective vs. generalized; info not permanently lost
  • Dissociative fugue = SPECIFIER (purposeful travel/wandering + identity amnesia)
  • Most amnesia/fugue resolves spontaneously without treatment
  • Depersonalization = self; Derealization = environment; reality testing INTACT (≠ psychosis)

Sexual Dysfunctions

  • DSM-5 lists alphabetically (dropped Masters & Johnson's 4-stage cycle model)
  • Psychogenic ED: nocturnal/morning erections PRESERVED
  • Physiologic ED: nocturnal erections typically ABSENT too

Paraphilias

  • Paraphilia = atypical sexual interest (ascertained by report/action)
  • Paraphilic DISORDER = paraphilia + distress/impairment/harm to others (diagnosed)
  • 8 named: fetishistic, transvestic, pedohebephilic, voyeuristic, exhibitionistic, frotteuristic, sexual sadism, sexual masochism
  • Voyeuristic/exhibitionistic/frotteuristic inherently involve a non-consenting party

Paraphilia Treatment & Hypersexuality

  • Tx: incorporation therapy, psychotherapy, orgasmic reconditioning, drug therapy (antiandrogens/SSRIs)
  • 4 who seek tx: court-ordered, self-distress, sexual dysfunction, (harm risk)
  • Hypersexuality red flags: brain injury, Klüver-Bucy, Kleine-Levin, dopamine agonists

Quick Differentiators

  • Somatic symptom vs. illness anxiety: real physical complaints dominate vs. fear/preoccupation dominates
  • Malingering vs. factitious: stops after external gain vs. persists regardless (sick role is the goal)
  • Factitious vs. somatic symptom: conscious/deliberate vs. unconscious
  • DID vs. dissociative amnesia: alternate identity states present vs. memory gaps alone
  • Depersonalization/derealization vs. psychosis: reality testing intact vs. impaired
  • Paraphilia vs. paraphilic disorder: interest alone vs. + distress/impairment/harm
  • Psychogenic vs. physiologic ED: nocturnal erections preserved vs. absent
  • OCD vs. OCPD (cross-reference): true obsessions/compulsions + ego-dystonic vs. none + ego-syntonic

🎯 Addiction & Non-Clinical Drug Use — High-Yield One-Pager

Condensed by learning objective — LO1 Dependence vs. Addiction · LO2 Dopamine Hypothesis · LO3–5 MOA / Intoxication–Withdrawal / Management, grouped by drug class

LO 1 · Foundations

Core Distinctions

  • Addiction = biological mechanism (reward + maladaptive learning); not always substance-related
  • SUD = the diagnosable disease (DSM-5 criteria) a patient can have
  • Dependence = transient, need drug present for near-normal function → reversible with detox
  • Addiction = permanent structural/functional brain change → recovery is non-linear
  • Withdrawal = unmasking of dependence adaptations once drug is eliminated

Tolerance — 6 Types

  • Innate — pre-existing genetic/PK variation
  • Acquired PK — ↑CYP enzymes/transporters
  • Acquired PD (acute) — ↓receptor #, altered channels/signaling
  • Acquired PD (chronic) — gene expression changes
  • Behavioral — learned compensatory behavior
  • Conditioned — cue alone triggers compensation (e.g., paraphernalia → bradycardia)

🧠 Mnemonic

"I don't use to get high, I use to feel normal" = baseline has drifted toward drug peak — the wave-graph shift.

LO 2 · Dopamine Hypothesis & Management Principles

Reward Circuit

  • VTA → nucleus accumbens is the shared final pathway for every drug class below
  • GABAergic VTA neurons normally inhibit dopaminergic neurons; drugs cause disinhibition → ↑DA
  • Positive reinforcement = reward; negative reinforcement = relief (dominates once dependent)
  • Conditioned cues (people/places/paraphernalia) trigger craving without any drug present

Detox Goals & Tools

  • Withdraw agent (usually taper) → restore homeostasis → treat comorbidities → prepare for recovery
  • Clonidine (α2-agonist): blunts sympathetic surge in most withdrawal — NOT sufficient alone for depressant withdrawal seizures
  • Pharm alone ≈ drop in the bucket without psychosocial tx (CBT, AA/NA)

DSM-5 Comorbidity Pattern

Alcohol and sedative/hypnotics touch nearly every psychiatric diagnostic category (psychotic, bipolar, depressive, anxiety, sleep, sexual, delirium, neurocognitive) — broadest comorbidity footprint of any class.

LO 3–5 · Opioids

Opioids — Quick Reference

  • MOA: μ-agonism → VTA GABAergic disinhibition → ↑DA
  • Intox: euphoria, ↓gag, pinpoint pupils → poisoning: ↓resp. drive → apnea (cause of death)
  • Withdrawal: "worst flu ever" — cramps/diarrhea/myalgia/mydriasis/autonomic surge; NOT life-threatening
  • Naloxone: competitive antagonist; AE = precipitated withdrawal, arrhythmia (rapid IV), flash pulm. edema
  • Methadone: full agonist, oral, QT-prolongation risk
  • Buprenorphine: partial agonist, ceiling, lower OD risk
  • Suboxone (4:1 bup:nx): naloxone not oral-bioavailable — misuse deterrent by route
  • Naltrexone: antagonist, requires prior detox (unlike alcohol use)
LO 3–5 · Alcohol & Other Depressants

Alcohol

  • MOA: ↑GABA-A, ↓NMDA acutely; chronic use ↓GABA-A, ↑NMDA(NR2B)
  • Withdrawal: minor sx → hallucinosis/seizures (24–48h) → DTs (peak ~day 2, up to 7d) — most dangerous withdrawal in this lecture
  • Screening: AUDIT-C (scored 0–12); CAGE (2+ yes = positive)
  • Detox: long-acting benzos (diazepam, chlordiazepoxide) — symptom-triggered vs. front-loaded
  • Naltrexone (can start while still drinking) · Acamprosate (NMDA antag./GABA-A agonist, TID) · Disulfiram (blocks ALDH → acetaldehyde accumulation → aversive hangover)

Benzos vs. Barbiturates

  • Both act GABA-A, different sites — benzos have a real ceiling, barbs do NOT (more dangerous)
  • "Overdose-proof" benzo claim is false — still fatal in combination with other depressants
  • Flumazenil reverses benzo effects (incl. paradoxical excitation); no antidote for barbiturates — alkalinize urine (ion trapping)
  • Barbiturate withdrawal: delirium + life-threatening CV collapse → inpatient monitored detox
LO 3–5 · Stimulants

Cocaine & Amphetamine

  • Cocaine: Na-channel block + blocks DA/NE/5-HT reuptake (DAT most potent) → tactile hallucinations, cardiac risk, septum/gum damage
  • Amphetamine: reverses DAT + reuptake inhibition + MAO inhibition; withdrawal includes "existential crisis"
  • No FDA-approved tx for either; desipramine/fluoxetine reduce craving only

Nicotine & Caffeine

  • Nicotine: nAChR agonism, VTA positive-feedback loop; short t½ + inhalation → outsized addiction despite mild intox.
  • Varenicline (partial α4β2 agonist), bupropion (↓seizure threshold), NRT (stepdown)
  • Caffeine dependence in as little as 1 week; withdrawal = headache/fatigue, onset 12–24h, up to 1 week
LO 3–5 · Cannabinoids, PCP, MDMA, LSD & Designer Drugs

Quick Picks

  • Cannabinoids: THC → CB1 agonism; mild withdrawal; CUD increasingly recognized
  • PCP: NMDA antagonist; analgesia masks injury; vertical + horizontal nystagmus = signature finding
  • MDMA: reverses SERT → 5-HT flood → serotonin syndrome; delayed hyponatremia from polydipsia
  • LSD: 5-HT agonist; not addictive; talk-down > pharmacotherapy
  • Designer drugs/adulterants: treat the toxidrome, not the label; xylazine → medetomidine shift

Master Reference — Every Named Agent in This Lecture

AgentClassMOAPrimary Use / Note
NaloxoneOpioid antagonistCompetitive μ-blockerOpioid poisoning reversal — dose to restore breathing, not to "punish"
